anomalies.observed: Q1, the P-channel ideal-diode pass FET, has its source (Q1.2) on +5V and its drain (Q1.3) on USBC_VBUS_IN. U6 (LTC4412) has VIN (U6.1) on USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE (U6.6) on +5V. The other P-channel high-side switches (Q6, Q9) put the source on the +5V input and the drain on the switched output.
anomalies.expected: For the LTC4412 ideal-diode OR-ing arrangement, the FET source should be on the input supply (USBC_VBUS_IN, the VIN side) and the drain on the protected load (+5V, the SENSE side). The body diode should then conduct from VBUS toward +5V and block reverse current.

evidence.quote: USBC_VBUS_IN [High Power] : J3.A4(VBUS,passive) ... Q1.3(D,passive) R11.1(passive) R64.2(2,passive) U25.5(VBUS,passive) U6.1(VIN,power_in)

anomalies.impact: USB power may not reach +5V through the intended path. Current can flow from +5V back toward VBUS through the FET body diode, so the USB power path and reverse-current protection would not behave as designed.

anomalies.observed: The second LED of dual LED D30 has its anode A2 (D30.4) on ESTOP_OUT. Its cathode K2 (D30.2) goes through R60 to Net-(D30-K2), and R60.2 is also on ESTOP_OUT. Both LED2 terminals therefore sit on the same net, so the LED is shorted and R60 forms a loop from ESTOP_OUT back to itself.
anomalies.expected: The LED channel should span two different nets, with its anode and cathode on separate potentials so it can indicate ESTOP_OUT state, as the matching channel for D30.3/D30.1 does.

evidence.quote: ESTOP_OUT : D30.4(A2,input) J13.6(Pin_6,passive) J2.6(Pin_6,passive) R60.2(passive) U36.4(Y,output)

anomalies.impact: The ESTOP_OUT indicator LED never lights, and R60 carries no current, so the e-stop status indication is lost.

anomalies.observed: R13 is 27R in series with green LED D12 from +3V3. The driver U18.4 sinks the current through the LED.
anomalies.expected: A green indicator LED on 3.3V normally has a series resistor in the hundreds of ohms range, sized so the LED current stays near 2–10 mA. Other indicator LEDs on this board use 56R to 1k (R1, R15, R2, R3).
anomalies.impact: About 44 mA through D12 is high for a 0805 indicator LED and above what the open-drain buffer U18 can sink comfortably, which risks LED and driver overstress.

parsed.summary: The netlist and SPICE deck agree, so the anomaly must be found in the connectivity itself. The most likely defect is Q1 with source and drain reversed relative to the LTC4412 USB power-path arrangement. The D30 channel-2 LED shorted on ESTOP_OUT and the 27R LED current-limit value are lower-confidence findings.
